_about: The beat: which stories the engine brings Krish and which it leaves out. Ruling (Krish, 2026-11-24): the engine brings stories in his focus sectors (media, entertainment, content, arts, music, creator tech, with the economics of AI inside them) and not governance, regulation, security or data breaches. Ruling (Krish, 2026-11-25): sports is a focus sector too, beside the creative, arts, music, entertainment and media industries. Read by apps/control-plane/api/_beat.ts (the headline gate for the feed, the radar, investigations, creator posts and shift detection; avoid terms refuse a headline outright, focus terms keep a focus-sector headline that the release, launch or partnership rule would otherwise drop, and an enterprise productivity headline is kept only with a focus-sector angle), apps/control-plane/api/feed/ingest.ts (pool_categories_off_beat), apps/control-plane/api/_editorialRadar.ts (the lens prompt's beat block) and scripts/post-pack/idea_checks.py offbeat_findings (the Sunday gate, code off_beat: a board option on the avoid list with no focus-sector angle is refused). The reader row (his approved North Star reader line, 2026-11-26) is read by apps/control-plane/api/_relevance.ts, the judge roster and scripts/post-pack/humour_check.py; economics_keywords by the story score. focus_sectors[].entities are each sector's named companies, bodies, platforms, guilds, leagues and venues (real names only), read with the keywords by the story score's fit axis only (scripts/post-pack/story_score.py focus_in; Ruling, Krish, 2026-11-26): a topic that names one is in that sector. A keyword or an entity is a row here, never code. A keyword ending in * matches any ending (royalt* matches royalty and royalties); not_when phrases are taken out of the text before its keywords are read, so 'job security' is not a security story and 'state of the art' is not an art story. lens.ruling: Businesses first, and under the hood: the ideas board leans back to businesses and how AI is changing the way they work, inside the focus sectors, and away from individual creators.
lens.line: Businesses first, and under the hood. Each Monday, Wednesday and Friday option is about a business in these industries (a label, studio, publisher, broadcaster, streamer, platform, agency, club or league) or the AI companies, tools and markets they run on, and says what AI is changing in how that business works: how the work is made, sold, priced, licensed or paid for. An individual creator, artist or performer, or one creator tool's new feature, leads at most one option a day, and only when the story is what it shows about how the business around them works.

subjects.business: The story is about a company, an industry or a market and what AI changes in how it works: a label's licensing deal, a studio's pipeline, a broadcaster's ad model, a platform's pay-out rule, an AI firm's price that a whole sector runs on.
subjects.creator: The story is about one person (a creator, artist, musician, performer, writer, designer, director or athlete) or one tool feature launched for them, told through what they made or can now do.

reader._about: Who the publication is for: Krish's approved North Star reader line, verbatim, and the one wording every prompt reads for that reader. Read by apps/control-plane/api/_relevance.ts (intro, keep_line, media_line, buyer_test), apps/control-plane/api/_judges/roster.ts through _beat.ts READER (judges.reader and judges.buyer) and scripts/post-pack/humour_check.py (audience_short, the humour engine's audience; about, what a script is about); about is also read by scripts/post-pack/divergent.py (the repeat guard's problem line) and scripts/post-pack/meme_templates.py. The goals, numbers and channels do not change; only the reader narrows. Changed only by a pull request carrying his ruling.
lines: By December 2027, makeyourmindup is the publication the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media and sports industries pay to read on what AI is doing to how their work makes money. 50,000 people who make the calls or make the work read it, and the publication is worth owning on its own.

reader.ruling: The reader narrows to people who make the calls or make the work in the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media and sports industries. The old reader, a commercial leader who might hire Krish for thirty days to build an AI brain or an AI go-to-market plan, is retired from the relevance filter and the judges.
reader.about: what AI is doing to how work in the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media and sports industries makes money
reader.audience_short: People who make the calls or make the work in the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media and sports industries: smart, busy, not AI specialists
reader.intro: Its reader: people who make the calls or make the work in the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media and sports industries, reading on what AI is doing to how their work makes money.
reader.keep_line: - "keep": on the beat for that reader. An AI / agents / LLM story is kept when it reaches how work in the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media or sports industries is made, sold, watched or paid for, or when it moves the economics of AI those industries live inside (what models and tools cost, platform and marketplace dynamics, the builder economy, agents doing creative work). AI news with no line into those industries is not the beat: prefer "not_interesting" for it over "keep".
reader.media_line: Advertising, marketing and adtech are in bounds as the money of media: how a publisher, broadcaster, streamer, platform, creator, club or league is paid for attention. Consumer, retail and DTC stories are kept only when they carry a creative, arts, music, entertainment, media or sports angle.

buyer_test.line: - "not_interesting": on-topic for AI, but there is nothing here the reader would DO anything with. The reader makes the calls or makes the work in the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media or sports industries: the people who run a label, studio, publisher, broadcaster, club or league, and the musicians, artists, writers, performers, athletes and creators whose work it is. Ask: does this change how that person makes the work, prices it, licenses it, gets paid for it, hires for it or builds with AI? Mark not_interesting for AI news with no line into those industries, and for a one-off item with no second-order consequence: a personnel move, a version bump, an event listing, a quoted tweet, a syndicated video interview, a vendor announcement that repriced nothing.
buyer_test.register_line: His words for what he wants instead: "fun, and observant, and tying together multiple threads, shifts or themes, not just crappy unimportant one off news items". And for the register: "My tonality is commercial, positive, and visionary", not "governance, risk, safety, negative things, and overly technical things".
buyer_test.unsure_line: Only mark not_interesting when you are confident someone who makes the calls or makes the work in those industries would read it and have nothing to do differently.

reader.label: Reader
reader.question: Will the people this is written for actually read it?
reader.rubric: Score reach into the readership: people who make the calls or make the work in the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media and sports industries, from whoever runs the label, studio, publisher, club or league to the musician, artist, writer, performer, athlete or creator whose work it is. 10 means it speaks to something in their work or their money this quarter; 1 means it is for AI practitioners, generalist business readers, or nobody in particular. Do not reward flattery of that reader; reward usefulness to them. Judge the readership only. Whether one of them would pay for it is the paying-reader judge and not yours.
reader.evidence: Name who in those industries this lands with, and the situation they are in.

buyer.label: Paying reader
buyer.question: Would someone who makes the calls or makes the work in these industries pay for this?
buyer.rubric: Score paying reach: whether someone who makes the calls or makes the work in the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media or sports industries would pay for this, because it tells them something about how their work makes money that they could not get free elsewhere this week. 10 means they would forward it to their boss; 7 means they would pay to keep reading a publication that runs it; 4 means it is useful, but they could find the same thing free this week; 1 means it is free news they already saw. Judge paying reach only. Whether the wider readership reads it belongs to the reader judge, and the two of you disagreeing on one idea is a finding rather than a fault.
buyer.evidence: Name the person who would pay, the money in their work this tells them about, and why they could not get it free elsewhere this week.

ruling.said: On questions 1 and 3 I need your judgement in detail. I want a high-quality flexible engine that has learned from all its past mistakes and is upgraded now.
ruling.ruling: Kept, as the paying-reader judge. The North Star says these industries pay to read and the publication is worth owning on its own; no other judge tests pay-to-read, and the reader judge tests read-for-free. The old buyer (a commercial leader who might hire Krish within thirty days) tested the consultancy's buyer, which leaks across ventures, so it stays retired. The key stays buyer so stored verdicts, calibration and the check-judges invariants still join; every label says Paying reader. Its question is answered in the judges' accountability (config/judges.json review), never on faith.

offdays.line: Every off-day suggestion lives in the reader's world: the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media and sports industries, the people who make the calls there and the people who make the work. One with no line into those industries is off the beat, however funny or useful.
offdays.good_news: Good news is people in the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media and sports industries doing, earning or making more with AI: an artist, musician, performer, writer, creator or athlete, or the label, studio, publisher, broadcaster, club or league around them, named, with the number that shows it where there is one.
offdays.meme: A meme's subject is the reader's world: studios, labels, creators, clubs, leagues, artists, performers and fans, the shoot, the session, the tour, the matchday and the edit. Never office or enterprise AI: the inbox, the spreadsheet, the meeting, the boss and the copilot at work.
offdays.carousel: A carousel, a tip or a how-to is for someone who makes the calls or makes the work in those industries: a tool, a deal, a price or a move they can use in their own work this week.

refusals.dull: has no line into the creative, arts, music, entertainment, media or sports industries; every off-day suggestion lives in the reader's world (Ruling, Krish, 2026-11-26; config/beat.json offdays). Find its angle in those industries or replace it
